summary: SPY closed 715.87 on 11-19, 1.96% under its 730.19 200-day, after a -5.45% week. Realized vol has jumped to 23.7% (20d) from a 13.9% one-year norm and VIXY is up 30.7% in 5 days, so selling is spreading from Technology to every sector. Keep equity appetite low. Within the defensive sleeves, intermediate Treasuries are finally acting as a hedge. Gold and crypto are not hedging; they are being liquidated.
reasons: Regime is broken: SPY is 1.96% below its 200-day (715.87 vs 730.19), with 5d -5.45%, 21d -7.40% and 63d -6.28%. All three horizons are negative, so this is a trend and not one bad day.

Volatility is expanding: SPY 20-day realized vol is 23.67% against 13.90% over 252 days, and VIXY is +30.67% over 5d and +37.42% over 21d. At this vol a 5-session move of 1% or less is the least likely outcome, so I ruled out neutral and chose a direction.

Breadth has given way: RSP (equal weight) fell 4.12% in 5d and its 21d is now -2.31%. It still sits 1.70% above its own 200-day, but it is no longer holding up while the cap-weighted index falls. IWM is 5.18% below its 200-day (63d -11.69%).

Tech leads the decline: XLK 5d -7.53%, 21d -14.77%, 6.01% below its 200-day. QQQ 21d -11.05%, 5.42% below its 200-day. Every one of the 11 sector SPDRs is negative over 5d. The mildest is XLP at -1.32%.

Cross-asset deleveraging: gold (GLD 5d -5.55%, 21d -11.55%, 17.53% below its 200-day), BTC (21d -20.43%, 14.77% below its 200-day) and ETH (21d -21.94%) are falling with stocks while the dollar rises (UUP 21d +2.46%, 5.50% above its 200-day). That is what forced selling looks like, not rotation.

Duration is now hedging: TLT 5d +0.79% and IEF 5d +0.68% (21d +1.00%) rose in a week when SPY fell 5.45%. This reverses my 11-12/11-13 view that bonds were falling with stocks. Long yields are easing. TLT is still 2.77% below its 200-day, so the move is young.

What argues against risk-off: credit has not cracked. HYG is only -0.58% over 5d (21d -0.07%) and LQD +0.03% over 5d. A drop this sharp without credit stress can bounce hard. This is why confidence is 0.45 and not higher.

Track record: my risk-off calls on 11-09 and 11-12 graded right (-1.69% and -5.45%), the 11-06 one wrong (+2.59%), and both risk-on calls (11-10, 11-11) wrong. My hit rate is 0.556 against a 0.444 always-risk-off baseline. No Reviewer lesson in learning.json names the Market Analyst, so none shaped this call.

asset_class_view.equity_etfs: Risky. VOO 21d -7.42% and VTI 21d -7.05% are both about 2% under their 200-day (-1.95%, -2.05%), and QQQ is worse (-5.42%). International is no shelter: VXUS is 6.40% and VWO 9.40% below their 200-days, with 63d at -10.99% and -12.73%. VNQ is the least-bad equity sleeve (21d +2.16%, 0.34% below its 200-day) but still fell 3.34% over 5d through XLRE. Don't add equity beta. Because the regime filter is off, only defensive ETFs can be bought anyway.
asset_class_view.bonds_gold: Treasuries look like the better defensive choice now. IEF (21d +1.00%, 5d +0.68%, 1.36% below its 200-day, vol 5.1%) and BND (21d +0.58%, vol 4.1%) are rising while stocks fall. TLT does the same with more volatility (9.7%) and sits further under its 200-day (-2.77%). Gold is the weakest defensive sleeve: GLD is 17.53% below its 200-day with 252d vol of 29.3% and is falling with risk assets and against a strong dollar. Don't treat it as a hedge.
asset_class_view.crypto: Avoid. BTC is at about $61.9K, 14.77% below its 200-day (21d -20.43%). ETH is 17.68% below its 200-day (21d -21.94%, 63d -28.22%). Both are falling with equities and gold, and neither shows any sign of a bottom.

watch: SPY back above its 200-day (about 730) would move me to neutral or risk-on. A rebound of 1% or more that recovers less than half the 5.45% weekly loss would not.

HYG breaking lower (5d worse than about -1.5%, or a widening gap below its 200-day from -1.22%) would confirm risk-off and raise confidence. HYG holding flat while VIXY's 5d gain fades would point to a bounce.
RSP falling below its 200-day (now +1.70%) would mean the selloff has spread from Tech to the whole market.
If TLT and IEF turn back down along with stocks, my point that duration is hedging again is wrong and the defensive preference moves to cash and short duration (SHY 5d +0.30%).
If XLP (21d +3.16%, 6.68% above its 200-day) breaks with the rest, Staples is no longer a favored tilt.
